chunks: What Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man from your followers, from among their righteous ones, complained to me about what he suffers from sleep. He said: I intend to rise for salat of the night, but sleep overcomes me until morning comes. Sometimes I make up my prayer for a whole consecutive month or two months, bearing its burden. He said: Coolness of the eye for him, by Allah. He said: And he did not grant him permission to perform the prayer in the first part of the night, and he said: Making it up during the day is better.

I said: Among our women are virgin girls who love good and its people, and are eager for the prayer, but sleep overcomes them until morning. Sometimes they make it up, and sometimes they become too weak to make it up, while they are stronger for it in the first part of the night. So he granted them permission to perform the prayer in the first part of the night if they became weak and neglected the make-up.

key_terms.أَوَّلِ اللَّيْلِ: the first part of the night, before the usual preferred time of the night prayer
key_terms.النَّوْمِ: sleep that prevents a person from rising for worship
key_terms.الْقَضَاءُ: making up an act of worship after its preferred time has passed
key_terms.صَلَاةِ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer performed as a recommended act of worship
key_terms.ضَعُفْنَ: they became weak or unable to fulfill the later performance or makeup

ai.seo_question: When is it permitted to perform Salat al-Layl at the beginning of the night instead of after midnight?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on the time of nawafil of the night for those who are overcome by sleep. It distinguishes between a man who can consistently make up Salat al-Layl during the day, for whom daytime makeup is preferable, and young women who may miss both the night prayer and its makeup, for whom praying earlier in the night is permitted.
